description: A curriculum director must approve the operating details of a new interdisciplinary college course, including its delivery format, instructional hours, assessment, course coding, and learning-material access, with input from the faculty sponsor, registrar, and copyright librarian.

shared_context.S1: The college is reviewing a proposal for a new three-credit interdisciplinary course called Community Data and Public Life.
shared_context.S2: The draft proposal describes an eight-week hybrid course with a final examination, 30 contact hours, course code INT-200, and learning materials posted on the public course website.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Priya Nair has authority to approve the course's operating details before it is published in the catalog.
shared_context.S4: As part of the college's normal course-review process, Dr. Nair asks the faculty sponsor, registrar, and library representative for any information that should be reflected before approval.

PF1.text: Professor Morales ran a pilot of the course this term and found that students must complete exactly 20 hours of supervised community fieldwork; the pilot also showed that a faculty-reviewed portfolio is required instead of a final examination. She completed the pilot report yesterday, but the proposal file still contains the earlier draft.

PF2.text: The confirmed transfer-articulation record assigns this course code INT-205 and requires exactly 45 instructional contact hours for the three-credit equivalency. Marcus received the record from the partner college yesterday, but has not entered the changes in the catalog workflow.

PF3.text: The publisher license for the course case materials permits access only to enrolled students through the college's password-protected e-reserve system and prohibits posting the materials on a public website. Jamal confirmed the license terms with the publisher this week, but the proposal still lists public posting.

acceptance_conditions: The course must include exactly 20 hours of supervised community fieldwork.
The course must use a faculty-reviewed portfolio instead of a final examination.
The course must provide exactly 45 instructional contact hours.
The catalog course code must be INT-205.
Course materials must be available only to enrolled students through password-protected e-reserve.
A fieldwork-and-assessment implementation commitment must be recorded.
A registrar catalog-update commitment must be recorded.
A copyright-compliant materials commitment must be recorded.
The faculty sponsor's pilot finding must be cited in the decision justification.

decisive_facts.why: The pilot report changes fieldwork from the draft's unspecified amount to exactly 20 hours and changes assessment from a final examination to a faculty-reviewed portfolio.
The transfer-articulation record changes the instructional requirement from 30 to exactly 45 contact hours and changes the catalog code from INT-200 to INT-205.
The publisher license changes materials access from public posting to enrolled-student password-protected e-reserve and requires a copyright-compliant implementation record.
